subject: KitePay inference impact — findings, timeline, and corrective plan
messages:
From: ops@kitepay.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@kitepay.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service errors during inference (high 5xx and token truncation)

Hi Jonas —

We started seeing intermittent 502/504 responses from Redwood around 08:45 PDT and a pattern of token truncation in generated outputs that caused failed transactions for ~12% of requests. Customer-facing timeout pages were triggered for a subset of our merchants.

What we observed: 
- Elevated 5xx rate (502/504) on /v1/generate endpoints between 08:45–09:05 PDT.
- Shortened outputs where generation stopped mid-sentence (~11:20–11:35 UTC).
- No change on our side. We did not deploy anything and only restarted a small batch of workers.

We need: timeline, root cause, and what you're doing to prevent recurrence. This is high priority for KitePay ops.

Attaching the client request traces we captured (attachment: kitepay_client_traces.zip).

—Maria Gonzalez
Head of Ops, KitePay
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: ops@kitepay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service errors during inference (high 5xx and token truncation)

Maria —

Thanks for the quick signal and the traces. I'm pulling the runtime team into a bridge now and we'll run live diagnostics; we'll follow up with a short timeline and an immediate mitigation plan within 90 minutes.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Triage on runtime node metrics and kernel logs (laura is on this).
- Enable a temporary routing fallback to the last-known-good model variant for your account to reduce 5xx rates.
- Preserve all logs/kv caches for postmortem.

Could we schedule a 30-minute call at 10:15 PDT so we can share findings live? If that works, we'll send a calendar invite.

I know this impacted some merchant flows — we'll include compensation options if SLA breach is confirmed.

Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: ops@kitepay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Findings and corrective plan — KitePay Aug 9 partial outage

Maria / KitePay Ops —

Thanks again for being on the call earlier. Below is a concise, customer-facing summary of our investigation, timeline, root cause, and the actions we're committing to. We've kept technical detail at a level for your SRE and product teams; happy to expand any section.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Incident window: 2027-08-09 08:45–11:30 PDT. Impact: elevated 5xx responses on /v1/generate and truncated outputs affecting ~12% of KitePay inference traffic.
- Root cause (short): a rare kernel-space memory reclamation event on a subset of dedicated serving hosts caused intermittent process stalls and KV cache corruption that led to token truncation and failed request handling.

Detailed timeline (key events)
- 08:41 PDT — small spike in request queue latency; minor backlog starts on 3 dedicated hosts serving KitePay.
- 08:45 PDT — customers observe first 502/504s; our alerting fires for elevated 5xx.
- 08:50–09:00 PDT — runtime team observes repeated context switch stalls; initial mitigation: throttle concurrent long-sequence batches for affected hosts.
- 09:05 PDT — we re-routed KitePay traffic to a fallback model variant and cleared backlog; visible 5xx rate drops by ~70%.
- 09:20 PDT — truncated outputs observed; debugging shows corrupted KV cache entries on two hosts.
- 10:10 PDT — full snapshot of kernel logs indicates an OOM/kernal reclaim cycle tied to a specific GPU driver path under rare memory fragmentation.
- 11:30 PDT — all hosts recovered after rolling restart and cache rebuild; traffic normalized.

Root cause analysis (concise)
- Primary cause: an unusual interaction between our serving runtime's continuous caching layer and a GPU driver memory fragmentation pattern that, under sustained long-sequence batching, allowed kernel memory reclaim to trigger without timely process preemption on a small set of hosts. This led to transient corruption of cache metadata and subsequent token streaming truncation.
- Contributing factors: higher-than-typical long-sequence batching on KitePay’s workload that increased memory pressure; lack of a kernel-level guard in our packaging to preempt this particular reclaim path.

Immediate mitigations completed (actions already taken)
- Rerouted traffic to validated fallback model variants for KitePay within 20 minutes of alert.
- Performed rolling restarts on affected hosts and rebuilt KV caches.
- Temporarily limited concurrent long-sequence batches for KitePay routing to reduce memory pressure.

Planned corrective actions (timeline & owners)
- Short term (next 72 hours):
  - Patch runtime to add defensive checks around KV cache metadata writes and enable a guard flag that forces preemption before kernel reclaim in high-fragmentation scenarios. Owner: Runtime Eng (Laura Bennett).
  - Deploy updated GPU driver + container runtime configuration to affected pool and run a soak test. Owner: Infra Eng (Vivek Kulkarni).
  - Add per-customer batching limits exposed as a configurable policy so we can tune without redeploys. Owner: Platform Eng.
- Medium term (2–6 weeks):
  - Instrument finer-grained kernel and memory fragmentation metrics and add automated rollback triggers for model routing. Owner: Observability.
  - Expand our eviction-safe KV cache serialization to prevent metadata races. Owner: Runtime Eng.

Customer impact & remediation
- We will proactively apply a one-time service credit if the incident meets the SLA criteria. Our billing team will follow up with a draft credit calculation and proposal by Aug 16.
- If you would like a private technical deep-dive (Jira-level), we can schedule a 60–90 minute session with runtime engineers and driver specialists.

Attachments (provided): kitepay_incident_timeline.csv; serving_runtime_kernel_logs.zip; k8s_pod_descriptions.txt.

Next steps (for KitePay)
- Confirm whether you want the deep-dive session; propose Monday 08/16 or Tuesday 08/17.
- Share any additional traces or downstream errors you still observe — we will correlate.

Again, apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience. We're treating this as a high priority and will keep you updated on the progress of the short-term fixes.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: KitePay incident — follow-ups, asks, and exec summary

Laura / Vivek —

Thanks for the rapid response today. Summary of items I need from each of you by EOD tomorrow: 

Laura (Runtime Eng) —
- Provide the patch diff for the KV cache defensive write and an estimate for a canary rollout (ETA: 72 hours).
- Confirm any required code changes to our serialization path and list the test coverage gaps.

Vivek (Infra) —
- Confirm exact driver version combinations observed in the affected pool and the plan to bake the updated config into the host images (ETA: 48–72 hours).
- Prepare a short soak test plan and acceptance criteria.

Other asks: 
- Billing: start a draft credit calc for KitePay and share with me (cc to customer support) by Aug 16.
- SRE: add a dashboard tile for host-level kernel reclaim metrics and set an automated paging threshold.

I'll coordinate a customer deep-dive once we have the short-term patch and a clear rollout plan. Please add any other action items to the attached commitment_tracker.xlsx.

Jonas
